Introduce the HDD Office package at the same existing launch: baseline excludes Abacus 3, the November software option is conditional, and the later networking option requires separately selected compatible software. Migrate the previously undated network revision from version 2 to version 3 and insert the November option as version 2; no live record pins the old product version 2, and its snapshot is retained in review evidence. Keep COMDEX 1980 as an explained later demonstration. Shared launch/campaign records make these edits atomic. Also remove obsolete source-file wording and Academy purchase-credit/tuition wording from the affected launch and its process, following the instruction to keep commercial pricing outside this model. No event date, technical BOM target or authorization is invented.

stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

Michael Douglas

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration.
Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence.
Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.
Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases.
Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.
Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate.

before.title: Artemis platform launches commercially
before.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support. Introduces Artemis training. At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance. The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts. Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required. Logix introduced an Artemis 128 KiB office configuration with two floppy drives, a Color Monitor II, keyboard, AIONix, Business Tools and one year of support. A second configuration added a 5 MB disk subsystem. Customers could add Abacus 3 from November 1980 and networking from May 1981.

outcomes.description: Launch campaign and dated follow-up activities are specified in ncc_1980_campaign.json and NCC_1980_CAMPAIGN.md. Compatibility through 2000 is a commitment with eligibility and maintenance obligations, not evidence of future fulfilment.

The launch includes the Artemis 128 KiB budget office configuration with two floppy drives, Color Monitor II, keyboard, AIONix, Business Tools and one year of support, plus an alternative adding a 5 MB disk subsystem. Abacus 3 can be added from November 1980 and networking from May 1981.

marketing_content.description: After the 55-minute presentation
Aurelia+
Artemis

Identical vector transformations and fixed-point precision, inputs, rounding and verified output; time computation separately from rendering and I/O. Publish source, compiler options, configuration and repeat-run range.
Same shaded rotating cube, geometry and image quality; identify display hardware, frame-buffer and display-transfer costs separately. Do not infer pure CPU speed from unequal graphics systems.
Publish measured ratios only after reproducible qualification; no forecast assumes an unmeasured speed multiplier.

Incremental qualified 80×40 and 80×25 high-resolution text demonstrations, grayscale bitmap/sprites, explicit old-monitor limitations and replaceable card. Retain existing presentation duration; incorporate into Artemis product demonstration.
